Ok, disabling AI detection is one way, but means less security. Isn't there a way to customize it?
I’ll check GitHub’s current options for tuning AI detection, including exclusions and any controls for individual rules.

content.text:
**Partly. I should have checked the narrower options first.** GitHub exposes an on/off switch for AI detection, but no documented controls for its prompt, sensitivity, or “ignore SHA-256 hashes” rules. [GitHub API docs](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/repos/repos)

There are two practical alternatives:

- **Path exclusions:** `.github/secret_scanning.yml` can exclude transcript files. However, those exclusions also suppress standard secret alerts and push protection for those files, potentially hiding real leaked keys. [Exclusion docs](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/how-tos/secure-your-secrets/customize-leak-detection/exclude-folders-and-files)
- **Targeted automatic dismissal:** Re-enable AI detection and add automation that closes only password alerts whose surrounding content proves they are package hashes or session identifiers. Unrecognized password findings and provider-token alerts stay open. GitHub supports closing alerts through its API. [Alert API](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/secret-scanning/secret-scanning)

**I recommend targeted dismissal for this repo.** All the alerts we checked came from checkpoint transcripts, but excluding transcripts entirely would remove useful coverage. This would customize alert handling rather than GitHub’s detector, so alerts may briefly appear before dismissal.

AI detection is still disabled; I haven’t changed anything further.
AI detection will stay disabled. Standard secret scanning and push protection remain enabled.

content.text: Dependabot PR #333 already fixes all four alerts by upgrading urllib3 to 2.8.0 and multidict to 6.9.1. Its latest head now has all 32 checks passing and is mergeable. These dependencies are used by the benchmark harness, including the nightly workflow; they aren’t part of the shipped Go CLI.

**Four open alerts remain. All affect Python benchmark dependencies, rather than the shipped Go CLI.**

| Alert | Severity | Issue | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| [#12](https://github.com/entireio/entire-graph/security/dependabot/12) | High | HTTPS proxy TLS verification can be overridden | urllib3 2.8.0 |
| [#13](https://github.com/entireio/entire-graph/security/dependabot/13) | High | Malicious streamed responses can exhaust memory | urllib3 2.8.0 |
| [#14](https://github.com/entireio/entire-graph/security/dependabot/14) | Medium | Deflate streaming can loop indefinitely | urllib3 2.8.0 |
| [#17](https://github.com/entireio/entire-graph/security/dependabot/17) | Medium | Certain multidict set operations leak memory | multidict 6.9.1 |

These are valid dependency vulnerabilities. The benchmark nightly workflow installs the affected versions, although exploitation requires the specific usage described in each advisory.

**[PR #333](https://github.com/entireio/entire-graph/pull/333) already fixes all four.** Its current head (`271093d8`) has:

- All 32 checks passing.
- No merge conflicts and no outstanding blocking findings.
- All Entire gates passing, including your recorded approval.

I recommend merging #333. I left the alerts open and made no changes. This assessment used source, advisories, and current CI evidence; I didn’t run exploit reproductions.
